title: Tenali Raman Tale 96 (తెలుగు)

full_text:
An impoverished farmer named Mallesh came weeping to the court of Vijayanagara.
His neighbor, a wealthy and aggressive landholder named Bhupati, had secretly moved the ancient granite boundary stone dividing their properties twenty yards into Mallesh’s land during a moonless night, stealing three fertile acres of cotton fields!
When Mallesh protested, Bhupati claimed:
'The stone has stood in this exact spot for a hundred years! Look at how deeply it is embedded in the soil!'

The village council was intimidated by Bhupati’s wealth, and the King sent Tenali Raman to investigate.

Tenali inspected the granite boundary stone.
The stone was indeed set deep in the earth, and the surrounding soil had been tamped down with water to look undisturbed.
Tenali smiled calmly: 'Dig up the stone!'

The workers dug a trench around the stone and hauled it out of the ground.
Tenali examined the earth beneath the stone’s base:
The soil was loose, fresh, and underneath lay green, crushed grass that had not yet turned brown!
Grass crushed beneath a stone for a hundred years turns to black ash within three months; green grass proves the stone was placed there within forty-eight hours!

Furthermore, Tenali pointed to an ancient neem tree standing twenty yards away on the ridge:
'Look at the roots of this neem tree!
Tree roots grow away from heavy stone obstacles.
The ancient groove where the boundary stone rested for fifty years is visible twenty yards back, where the neem roots formed a deep hollow!'

Tenali ordered workers to dig at the old groove:
There, beneath the soil, was the original foundation bed of river gravel and pottery shards laid by the village founders fifty years before!

Faced with undeniable archaeological and botanical evidence, the landholder turned pale and confessed his crime.
King Krishnadevaraya restored the stolen land to Mallesh, fined Bhupati one hundred gold coins, and had the boundary stone set permanently in iron-reinforced mortar.
The people celebrated Tenali Raman’s keen deductive eye, which saw truth buried beneath the surface of the earth.
moral: Greedy neighbors who shift boundary stones under the cover of night are caught by the patient memory of roots. [TE]
